## Editor-facing mission: generalize the ORIGINAL mechanism without altering its results

This is a **research-only Draft** child of R15, not a submission or a proposed merge into original PR #34. The original R9 model, original Cournot Propositions, residual-cost formula, coalition-stability results, original numeric witness, supplementary proofs and historical negative tests are preserved **byte-for-byte** as predecessor content. Page count is deliberately deferred.

## Actual theoretical advance, not generic profit relabeling

- R12+R13 gave **one conduct-neutral sufficient-condition mechanism** for (G1) endogenous SU outsider-only private compatibility and SW no-adoption, and (G3) a buyer-microfounded *integrated national-incidence* criterion for government preference reversal, robust even when the marginal national-welfare effect changes sign.
- **R9 Cournot** satisfies G1+G3 with exact certificates and has a nonempty infinite-dimensional nonlinear inverse-demand neighborhood (R15).
- **NEW R16 Bertrand** satisfies **the same G1 and G3** under an independent differentiated-quadratic, consumer-optimized fulfilled-network-expectations model. At (gamma,v,c,d,F)=(23/25,33/500,2/125,1/500,1/40), exact operating payoffs across ALL 8 SU/64 SW standard-support profiles show max member/SW adoption gain ~=0.01515717 < F=.025 < outsider gain ~=0.02981642. Member SU-minus-IS welfare changes **+0.00277400733 to -0.00090743389**. Consumer welfare is **correctly** CS=q'M0q/2, not previously erroneous R10 CS=q'(M0-vC)q/2.
- **Price-game verification exceeds interior FOCs:** Exact active-set profit maximization across 19 distinct network/cost markets, 211 feasible rational candidate deviations, and 171 strict profitable-entry inequalities rule out all unilateral profitable price deviations and every inactive-brand equilibrium. Thus the price equilibrium in each relevant market is globally Nash and unique.
- **R12-G3 IN BERTRAND:** Explicit symbolic compatibility/cost interpolation; positive Bernstein coefficients prove W''>0 on a continuum, and the exact **64-bin right-Riemann upper bound** -0.00280224531698 is below -G0=-0.00277400733148. Hence **the very same general theorem** drives the Bertrand ranking reversal, not merely an endpoint numerical coincidence.
- **Beyond quadratic demand:** Nonquadratic consumer utility U=1'q-q'M0q/2-epsilon sum(q_i^4)/4 with epsilon=1e-4, solved for every stage-market combination and investment deviation, retains SU-minus-IS ranking +0.00272947 before / -0.00090978 after. Research note presents a parameter-open and conditional C3 function-space continuation argument (requires hostile peer scrutiny on price-strategy compactification and global uniqueness).

## Important limits, no unsupported “perfect IJIO” claim

The Cournot and Bertrand nonvacuity examples use **different primitive parameter values** and differentiate products differently; R10's earlier **same-parameter** claim was withdrawn after R15 revealed inconsistent CS accounting. The general theorem is **conditional**; not all price games or demands induce the reversal, nor is standard national welfare incidence a newly invented math theorem. Original nearest literature must still be compared at proposition/proof level, especially Gandal & Shy (2001), Katz & Shapiro (1985), Walz & Woeckener (2003), Buccella–Fanti–Gori (2026) and strategic-trade pass-through research. IJIO editorial outcome is **not guaranteed**.

## Artifacts

- Append-only new Proposition in `paper/jict_short/short_04_incentives.tex` (all earlier R9-R15 text left untouched)
- Independent research gate and theorem proof: `research/r16/R16_CONDUCT_NEUTRAL_COURNOT_BERTRAND_GENERALITY_AUDIT.md`
- Exact price/welfare/adoption audit scripts, global rival-exit deviation scripts and the G3 exact Bernstein/Riemann certificate
- Nonlinear consumer-price example re-solving all market and firm-stage profiles
- Isolated GitHub Actions workflow to reproduce claims

**NO MERGE / NO JOURNAL SUBMISSION** without final referee-level source-theorem audit and explicit author approval. Length requirements are intentionally out of scope for now.

## Purpose
Carry out **source- and theorem-level** skeptical novelty assessment of the original IJIO project and its R16 generalization, not rewrite or weaken any existing result. Original R9 PR #34 and scientific sources R9–R16 are unchanged. Page count deferred.

## Research artifacts
- `research/r17/R17_ORIGINAL_NOVELTY_VS_R16_PRIMARY_THEOREM_ABSORPTION_AUDIT.md`: >30k-character primary-text / historical claim-ledger report mapping editor decision, R1/R2/R7/R9 novelty findings, R12–R16 new conditional G1/G3 theorems and documented original R10 retraction to **specific propositions** in parent works. Explicit source access classifications `[P]` full text vs `[A]` abstract; forbids firstness claims.
- `research/r17/R17_PROPOSED_MANUSCRIPT_POSITIONING.tex`: cautious proposed introduction paragraph distinguishing Gandal–Shy (2001) *already price competition, public standards unions*; Takarada et al. (2020) public regional/multilateral ranking; Buccella et al. (2023, **2026**) endogenous private compatibility/Cournot–Bertrand; Maggi–Mrázová costly adaptation after public standard-setting and formal agreements. Preserves original question; **not included in paper builder** until author approves.
- `research/r17/R17_PROPOSED_ADDITIONAL_REFERENCES.bib`: missing vetted Buccella–Fanti–Gori (2026) published citation and Walz–Woeckener (2003) CEPR working paper. Maggi 2024 key already in canonical BibTeX; no duplication.

## Most serious new finding
A **directly inspected Dec. 2024 Yale full version of Maggi–Mrázová** has governments set national exact emission standards followed by **firms' post-policy fixed-cost adaptation/supply of different standards**, and Propositions 1–2, 6–7 and Remark 5 explicitly show spontaneous standards harmony and formal agreements inducing greater diversity or being only coordinating. Thus 'government sets standards, then firm pays an extra-standards fee' is **NOT novel**. The remaining candidate R16 contribution is appreciably narrower: after an *already fixed exclusionary regional government coalition*, the outsider *alone* buys the member standard and thereby reverses the *same government member's counterfactual SU-vs-IS preference*, while members' own outsider-market disadvantage persists, with joint G1+G3 equilibrium-feasibility verified in Cournot AND Bertrand under consumer-consistent welfare.

## High-risk unresolved close predecessors
- **Maggi–Mrázová July 16, 2026 revised full paper** not inspected; 2024 author's Yale full PDF was inspected and is compared proposition-by-proposition.
- **Buccella–Fanti–Gori (2026)** full article behind publisher paywall; abstract shows one-way compatibility and Cournot/Bertrand are directly prior. The 2023 Pisa PDF is **another paper**, not this 2026 article.
- Walz–Woeckener (2003), Klimenko (2009): official full abstracts verified, full theorems not yet extracted.

## Verdict
**CONDITIONAL GO for R16's stronger generality argument, NOT originality-certified or IJIO resubmission-ready.** The novel candidate is the strict *cross-stage government-institution preference* effect; finite dominance, consumer choice microfoundation and national incidence identities are established theory individually. Exact price game checks alone cannot guarantee independent original IO insight. Further primary proof absorption and a tighter economic primitive theorem needed.

**DO NOT MERGE / SUBMIT:** journal choice and manuscript changes require separate author approval; PR #34 untouched. Source annotations in the audit include DOI and original-paper URLs.

## Independent R18 research result — no merge/submission

**Theorem status:** Main Proposition R18-P is a rigorously proven **conduct-neutral conditional mechanism**. It separately bounds (1) the initial member-market protection net of persistent export losses and (2) residual protection after one-way private support. It DOES NOT derive the signs of all derivative response envelopes directly from arbitrary consumer utility / production-cost / conduct primitives. **Level 2, NOT Level 3 or 4.**

### Actual new mathematical content
- Two-channel cost/compatibility decomposition (local protection b, compatible residual r, export handicap e, network contrasts H,J).
- Sufficient inequalities `c(bL-eU)>H+J` and `d*rU<J+c*eL` give SU-to-IS government ranking reversal without assuming either welfare ranking.
- Scope selection: `max(0,beta,sigma)<F<2alpha`; one outsider interface covers two member markets, member reverse access only one.
- Independently re-solved exact SymPy rational **8 SU + 64 SW** adoption profiles under both R9 Cournot and R16 differentiated Bertrand, including every firm investment deviation. New bounds strict in BOTH instances:
  - Cournot: pre lower +0.0011264283; post upper -0.0020701231.
  - Bertrand: pre lower +0.0013170012; post upper -0.0005916274.
- Inherited R16 global Bertrand price deviations / 2026 literature constraints stated **explicitly**; R18 did **not** independently re-run every global price deviation or establish all-C3 global uniqueness.
- Counterexample v=0,c=.1: pre advantage -47/3200, so not universal.

### Artifacts
Nine new files under `research/r18/`: model, theorems/proofs, primitive reduction, R9 exact nesting/preservation, novelty audit, independent hostile referees, SymPy executable, local verification log, manuscript proposal. One isolated `.github/workflows/r18-general-theorem-audit.yml`.

### Protection and priority
Created from R17 commit `786bbf43444d735b8dafabd41ceb1d05ac878525`. PR #34 original and all inherited `paper/`, `docs/`, `code/` sources are unchanged. R10 FE welfare correction/retraction remains in place. Gandal–Shy (2001), Maggi–Mrázová (2024/2026), Buccella–Fanti–Gori (2026), Walz–Woeckener (2003) overlap remains serious. 2026 full-text priority questions unresolved.

**No merge into parent research or JICT, no paper submission. Draft only.**
